text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on November 21 in history.
1694 - The French philosopher Voltaire born in Paris as Francois-Marie Arouet; he was famed for his "Candide" and "Lettres Philosophiques".
1695 - English composer Henry Purcell died from tuberculosis.

1783 - The first successful flight was made in a hot air balloon when Frenchmen Francois Pilatre de Rosier and Francois Laurent, Marquis d'Arlandes, flew for 25 minutes above Paris for a distance of some 5 1/2 miles (8 km).
1787 - Shipowner Samuel Cunard born in Nova Scotia; he later came to Britain and formed the Cunard Line in 1839.
1789 - North Carolina became the 12th state of the United States.
1854 - Pope Benedict XV born as Giacomo Della Chiesa; elected pope just after the outbreak of the First World War, he tried to maintain a policy of strict neutrality during the conflict.
1888 - Adolph Marx, second oldest of the Marx brothers comedy team and known as "Harpo", born.
1916 - Emperor Franz Josef died; ruler of the Austro-Hungarian Empire since 1848, his attack on Serbia helped precipitate World War One.
1918 - The German High Seas Fleet surrendered at the Firth of Forth in Scotland, one of the key conditions of the armistice signed on Nov 11.
1920 - The Irish Republican Army shot dead 14 British soldiers in what became known as the country's first "Bloody Sunday".
1942 - James Hertzog, South African statesman and Boer general, died; he was prime minister 1924-1939 and lost office over neutrality in World War Two.
1953 - The British Museum published a scientific report proving that the Piltdown Man discovery by Charles Dawson in 1912 was a hoax.
1974 - In the English city of Birmingham, 21 people were killed and 162 injured when bombs exploded in two pubs; the IRA claimed responsiblity.
1990 - Lebanon's strongest Christian militia agreed to surrender its Beirut stronghold, rescuing a bid by the Syrian- backed government to end 15-years of civil war.
1994 - NATO launched an unprecedented air strike against a rebel Serb-held airfield in Croatia, the biggest such raid in the alliance's 45-year history.
1995 - Parties at the Bosnia peace tallks in Dayton, Ohio, agreed to an accord ending the bloody Balkan conflict.
1995 - Acting Prime Minister Shimon Peres formed a new Israeli government following the assassination of Yitzhak Rabin.
1995 - China formally arrested Wei Jingsheng, its most prominent dissident and father of its embattled democracy movement.
1995 - King Norodom Sihanouk's half brother, Prince Norodom Sirivudh, was charged with plotting to kill Cambodian co-premier Hun Sen.
